context: Background workers consume jobs from a channel and publish results asynchronously. The service runs for hours in production.
explanation: The goroutine spawned by go p.publish(result, ch) is never awaited and ch is never read — if publish blocks on sending to ch, the goroutine leaks. Over hours of operation, leaked goroutines accumulate and exhaust memory. Fix: either await the goroutine via <-ch, or drop ch entirely and let publish run fire-and-forget without a blocking channel send.
